title: Importing a "Current" order flips the live Current order to non-modsettings, or overwrites a saved order
notes: Exporting Current writes Current.json, and import takes the name from the filename. DataContract restores only Order, so IsModSettings=false. SetFrom copies the false but keeps FilePath=modsettings.lsx, so Save writes JSON over modsettings.lsx and First() at MWVM:2967 throws. Branch B turns the selected saved order into a clone of Current and drops the import (memory only; .json on disk untouched).
fixCaveats: Current: FirstOrDefault(IsModSettings).SetOrder(order) and then LoadModOrder. Otherwise add the import as a new uniquely named order. [IgnoreSetFrom] is never read by SetFrom. Guard against a null SelectedModOrder. IsBaseLoadOrder hides the flip in the UI.

title: Importing a .bz2/.xz/.zst pak writes an empty file over the target
notes: TempFile.CreateAsync reads the decompression stream to the end. File.Create (3302) then truncates the target, and the second copy writes 0 bytes, yet success=true and the mod is added. The dialog and drag-drop accept these formats. Any existing file at the final path is truncated, not only <Folder>.pak.
fixCaveats: Seek(0) does not work: lslib's mmap uses leaveOpen=false, so disposing the pak closes the handle and DeleteOnClose deletes the temp file. Decompress to <target>.pak.tmp, load the metadata by path, File.Move(overwrite) on success, and otherwise delete the tmp.

title: Export cancellation races an abandoned writer and leaves a corrupt zip
notes: On cancel, Task.Delay(0, token) throws, and the using blocks dispose ZipWriter, which writes the central directory while the StartNew child still writes (DenyChildAttach). The in-flight entry is missing, the child's exception is swallowed, and the alert shows a stack trace. Users can reach this (Cancel visible). Downgraded to Medium: sources are untouched, so the result is a corrupt zip, not data loss.
fixCaveats: File.OpenWrite does not truncate, so a shorter export leaves the old tail. Use <out>.tmp with FileMode.Create and File.Move(overwrite). Handle OperationCanceledException with a neutral message, including the return false at 3595. Wrap File.OpenRead. The Directory.Delete at 3653 is not recursive and sits outside the try.

title: Archive import clobbers existing paks and leaves truncated paks behind
notes: File.Create in the Mods folder truncates any same-named pak immediately, with no check, prompt or temp file. On error or cancel the code only logs and the partial file stays. `success` is never reset per entry (3442), so a failed pak still loads after an earlier one succeeds. The plain .pak copy (1840-1845) also overwrites silently.
fixCaveats: Write to a .tmp file, validate it, File.Move(overwrite), and delete the tmp on failure. Reset success per entry. Apply the overwrite policy to the plain .pak path at 1845 too.

title: The E2 "collect failures and continue" fix would still ship truncated paks
location: MWVM:3677 -> SharpCompress Writers/Zip/ZipWriter.cs:83-86 and the ZipWritingStream.Dispose path (around 405-470)
notes: `using var output` around TransferTo means a read error mid-copy finalizes the entry with the partial CRC and sizes (ZipWriter.cs:399-447), leaving a valid zip with a truncated pak. Corrected statement: after E2 the exporter sees an alert, but the receiver cannot detect it. Rare on local disks, so Low.
fixCaveats: An exception after WriteToStream starts should abort the export and delete the temp/output file. Alternatively, compare the bytes written to the source length.

title: Pak loading is effectively serial despite Task.WhenAll (Stage 4 candidate)
docRef: plan Stage 4.2 candidates; plan-overview (9.3 s mod load)
notes: PackageReader.Read and the entry loop run synchronously before the first await. Uncompressed and Zlib reads finish synchronously, and only LZ4 moves work to the pool. The caller runs on TaskpoolScheduler, so the load is serial but does not block the UI. The 9.27 s step covers more than paks, so the gain needs profiling.
fixCaveats: Use Parallel.ForEachAsync or Task.Run per pak. Line 786 already logs the timing. Check that DivinityApp.Log is thread-safe, and note that the static _AllPaksNames is never cleared.

title: DivinityModData.Files retains every path of every pak and is never read (memory)
notes: Every pak load assigns a HashSet of all entry names to Files (DMDL:478, 488, 628). Nothing reads it: no code, no XAML binding, and no serialization (opt-in DataContract with no DataMember). wt-perf has the same code. The memory cost has not been measured.
fixCaveats: Removing the lines and the property changes no behaviour. Measure private bytes, or count entries across the 1,097 paks, to size the saving.

title: The builtin-mod load builds a full VFS over the Data paks to find about 30 base mods (Stage 4 candidate)
notes: Partly true. AttachGameDirectory reads the file tables of Game, Gustav, Shared and the language paks, and FinishBuild calls TryAddFile for every entry on each startup. Corrected statement: the 30 s token is never checked during the build, and metadataOnly skips the file table (PackageReader.cs:157), so it cannot be the fix. The cost has not been measured.
fixCaveats: A real fix has to read the file table, filter it for Mods/*/meta.lsx, and replace ModPathVisitor.DiscoverMods. Measure this step on its own in Stage 4.1 first.
